title: Set up a run of six dominoes on their ends along taped tick marks, then tip the first so all six fall in a chain
instruction: Stand all six dominoes on their short ends, one on each red tick in the taped lane, faces toward you. Then tip the domino nearest you away from you, touching no other domino, so that all six fall in a chain.
context: Standing dominoes on end in a line and knocking over the first is a familiar childhood game and a popular hobby. A domino standing on its 7.5 mm end tips over once it leans past 9 degrees, so each one has to be turned from lying flat to standing, set down square on its mark and let go of cleanly, and the hand must not brush the ones already standing 30 mm away; one careless touch topples them early. Then a single light push has to start the run. Standing thin items upright close to their neighbours without knocking them over is the same skill used in everyday tidying, such as setting books or cards upright on a shelf.
setup: Station table, one fixed layout. Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward (away from the arms), y to the left; heights above the table top. Dominoes: six tiles from a standard double-six domino set, each 48 x 24 x 7.5 mm, 10 g, ivory melamine with black pips (values 6|6, 5|3, 4|2, 6|1, 3|3, 2|0; any six tiles will do). They start lying flat, pip face up, long side along x, centres at x 215 and y +125, +175, +225 (left of the lane) and -125, -175, -225 (right of the lane), centres 50 mm apart side to side (26 mm gaps). Lane: two strips of 5 mm blue masking tape along x whose inner edges are 60 mm apart (y -30 and +30), and two across it whose inner edges are at x 190 and x 470, making a taped rectangle 60 mm wide inside. Ticks: six strips of 3 mm red fine-line tape across the lane (60 mm long), centred at x 220, 250, 280, 310, 340 and 370 (30 mm apart); tick 1 (x 220) is nearest the arms. Nothing else on the table. Both arms start in their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Scored every control step from the dominoes' poses; the score at the end of the trial counts. A domino stands on a tick when it is on its short end (long side within 10 degrees of vertical), its base on the table (within 3 mm), its base centre within 6 mm of the tick along the lane and within 8 mm of the lane's centre line, its broad faces within 15 degrees of square to the lane (one of them toward the arms; which face and which end is up do not matter), the robot not touching it (nothing within 1 mm), and no corner moving more than 1 mm over 0.5 s. 0.25: at some point three or more dominoes stood on distinct ticks at once. 0.5: at some point all six stood, one on each tick (the set). 0.75: in a clean run, at least the dominoes on ticks 1 and 2 fell forward. 1.0: in a clean run, all six fell forward, the last one lies flat (highest point at most 10 mm up), every corner of every domino is inside the tape's inner edges, no part of either arm is within 2 cm of any domino and nothing moves more than 1 mm, all held for 1 s (20 control steps). Otherwise 0. Fallen forward: its highest point at most 30 mm above the table (standing is 48 mm; stopped leaning on a standing neighbour, 46 mm) and its former top end pointing away from the arms (within 60 degrees of straight along the lane). Clean run, counted from the last moment of the set: the robot touches no domino but the one on tick 1, and does not touch that one once the domino on tick 2 leans 15 degrees; no domino starts to fall (15 degrees) before the one on the tick before it; in a real trial the robot also must not strike the table. A foul voids that run; standing all six up again starts a new one. So knocking them over by hand, pushing the first through the whole run or laying them out already fallen scores at most 0.5. In a real trial: a photo of the set (ruler against the ticks; a domino on its end touching nothing is within 9 degrees), a video of the run (touches, order; slow motion helps), and a ruler for the 30 mm and 10 mm heights and the tape edges.
reset_notes: Lay the six dominoes back flat, face up, at their starting spots (the screenshot and the setup give them). Nothing is consumed; the tape stays.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at real size and mass; no joints or scripted events: the chain is PhysX contact, gravity and friction (240 Hz). Each domino is one square-edged 48 x 24 x 7.5 mm, 10 g box, pips painted on; friction 0.40 static, 0.30 dynamic (estimates). Real tiles have rounded edges and tip a degree or two sooner. Touches come from the arms' collision hulls (within 1 mm). Tape is visual only; the table cannot be bumped.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (ran the full 2,400 steps); scripted demo: 1.0 (full score at step 1,411, episode ended with success at step 1,430)
